_about: The set and collection rules of the Scapes style as data, for core/set (planning, validation, generation). Every value here comes from the bible: SETS.md (and BASE_RULES.md, BACKGROUNDS.md), the section is named in `source` next to it; the bible is the authority, this file only makes its checkable rules readable by the program. windows: the window layouts of SETS.md 4.2–4.3 — stars per slot (`stars`, exact) or the order rule for a small window's own ladder (`stars_order`: non-decreasing | free) with the reference ladders as `examples`; `scenes`: allowed numbers of character scenes, always the tail of the window; `gold`: scenes = gold exactly on the scenes, none, items = gold only on cards without characters; `frame`: the frame of non-gold slots. abstract_when: the condition (prompt-assembly.json `when` syntax) for an abstract backdrop (SETS.md 3.7: a field or a wall with a pattern or gradient, not a wall of real material). stagings: the rows of BACKGROUNDS.md «Какую постановку выбрать», first match wins; `when` classifies an order's staging, `preset` is the staging a plan may start from (`{"preset": id, …fields}`), `fill` the fields the planner adds, `category` the categories the row gives (BACKGROUNDS.md «Категория как следствие постановки»: the first entry whose `when` matches, or any of the entries without `when`). collection: SETS.md 1.4 and 6.2 — 16 sets, the grand set last, the reference curve of scenes and the reference windows by position (the recommended sample). prompt: the text model's prompt for planning — `fragments` are the ids of the marked fragments of SETS.md «10. Для промпта (англ.)», `glue` is the program's own text around them (the JSON answer format, the collection split and the request for loose cards — `cards`, core/set/cards.js — which SETS.md has no fragment for).

contrast.source: COLOUR.md 7 (the hero's main colour and the backdrop's differ in hue by at least COLOUR.7 hue_diff_min of checks/thresholds.json, or clearly in lightness; an achromatic hero passes) and the fragment colour.hero-backdrop. A plan names colours only in words: `colours` maps a colour word to [hue in degrees, lightness class −1 dark | 0 middle | 1 light] by the usual sRGB colour of the name (the agent's table, not a bible measure); `lighter` and `darker` words before it shift the class. The hero's main colour is the first colour word of `palette` before its last " on "; the backdrop's is `hue`.

texture.why: ворс и мех стиль не рисует: формы гладкие, мех и руно — несколько круглых гладких завитков
texture.instead: a round, smooth body in soft matte colours

texture.why: сетки, плетение и тонкий узор стиль рисует несколькими крупными гладкими формами
texture.instead: one smooth, softly translucent piece, or a few thick, rounded bars

texture.why: износа и грязи у стиля нет: даже старые вещи чистые и свежеокрашенные
texture.instead: clean and freshly painted, with at most one or two simple paint chips

texture.why: зеркальный металл выходит фотографическим; у стиля металл крашеный или серо-голубой атласный, как у хорошей игрушки
texture.instead: painted toy metal with a few broad, soft highlights
simple clean surfaces in smooth soft gradients

orders.source: SETS.md 9.22–9.24: what the image model will read in a plan's orders — time of day, the backdrop against the hero, textures and materials

glue.system: You plan sets of collectible card illustrations for an image pipeline. Answer with one JSON object only, no prose.
glue.wishes:
The producer's wishes, which override any rule above: {wishes}
Carry them into the cards: let them shape each card's subject, environment, scene (time, action) and the scenes' staging time where they apply (item cards without characters stay in daylight), and write in each card's "wishes" one English sentence of what they ask of that card, said as what the viewer sees ("warm low morning sun, long soft shadows"; "small dark round eyes and a round, smooth body" rather than "no face"); "" when nothing in them concerns that card.
glue.slots: The window is fixed: {slots}. Fill every slot in this order; the cards with characters are the last {scenes} slots.
glue.answer: Answer as JSON: {"title": set name in one or two words, "angle": one line, "cards": [one object per slot, in slot order]}. A card object: "slot" (number), "kind" (the item kind in lower-case English, e.g. "fishing rod"; for a scene, the situation), "facet", "subkind", "caption", "object" (short English name of the hero, for a scene omit), "subject" (one English sentence describing the hero's look as this style draws it: shape, colours, parts, in simple smooth rounded toy-like forms; fur, fuzz, meshes, weaves and wear become a few bold smooth shapes and metal is painted toy metal with soft broad highlights; for a scene omit), "staging" ({"preset": one of the staging ids below, plus its fields}), "wishes" (only when the producer gave wishes: see below), "hue" and "palette" only for an item card on an abstract backdrop (presets field, smooth-floor, surface-patch, floor-or-furniture, wall): hue = the backdrop colour word, roughly opposite to the hero's main colour on the colour wheel (a blue object on golden yellow, an orange or red one on sky blue, a yellow one on violet, a red one on bright green, a green one on pink), palette = "a <hero colours> object on <hue>" with the hero's main colour first; neighbouring slots get different hues, "place" and "environment" (short English place and one sentence describing it in a few large simple masses, e.g. a broad lawn, rounded bushes and a few scattered flowers; needed for presets environment, native and scene), "motif" (small icon for pattern motif_repeat). A scene card also has "props" (item kinds visible in the scene) and "scene": {"theme", "time" (words, e.g. "at sunset"), "action", "item", "joke", "reactor", "jokeObject", "crop" (hips | waist | knees), "characters": [{"name": man | pig | cow | sheep | rooster, "costume": one English sentence}]}.
glue.stagings: Staging ids and the fields each needs: {stagings}. Allowed values: {values}. Time of day: item cards without characters are in daylight (time "day"); golden hour, dusk and night belong to scenes with characters, golden hour to at most two cards of a set.
glue.repair: Your plan broke these rules; answer with the whole corrected JSON plan: {errors}
glue.collection: Split the collection theme "{collection theme}" into {count} set themes: places, activities, trips, events, feelings, mixed. Each set theme gets its kind, a one-line angle and 5 to 6 example item kinds. Close themes are told apart by their angle (who owns the place, which environment, which stage of a trip) and share no item kinds. The last theme is the grand set: one celebration that sums up the collection, in one place. Order the sets so that kinds alternate and close themes stand apart. Answer as JSON: {"sets": [{"title", "kind", "angle", "examples": [item kinds]}]} with {count} entries, the grand set last.
glue.cards: Plan {count} loose collectible cards on the theme "{theme}" within the collection "{collection theme}": they are not a set, so there is no window, no stars and no frames. Spread them across the facets and sub-kinds of the theme; never two items of the same kind or the same purpose. {items} of them are item cards without characters, then {scenes} scenes with characters, last. Number the cards from 1 in "slot".
